# Map `machine`: spec v0 Part I (constraints), Parts II–III (§8–§20) vs draft `formal/Ern/MM02.lean`

Read-only mapping. Normative source: `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md` (frozen). Draft: `formal/Ern/MM02.lean` on `formal/derivability_0.1` (1576 lines, 91 theorems). All `file:line` below are on that branch. The draft compiles unchanged with Lean v4.35.0 (copy compiled at `scratchpad/ref/map/machine_check/MM02check.lean`); `#print axioms` on the key theorems gives at most `propext`, `Quot.sound`, plus `Classical.choice` for the four `*_total` theorems only.

Citation convention: `§N.k` = numbered item k of section N; `§N ¶p` = p-th paragraph of section N (a bullet list belongs to the paragraph that introduces it; `b`i = i-th bullet). Draft docstrings cite the old numbering of the v0.3 consolidated text; correspondence (verified against `~/Downloads/ERN_MM02_v04.md` headings): MM-01.0→§1, MM-01.1→§2, MM-01.2→§3, MM-01.3→§4, MM-01.4→§5, MM-01.5→§6, MM-01.6→§7, MM-02.1→§8, MM-02.2→§9, MM-02.3→§10, MM-02.4→§11, MM-02.5→§12, MM-02.A→§13, MM-02.E→§14, MM-02.B→§15, MM-02.C→§16, MM-02.D→§17, MM-02.F→§18, MM-02.G→§19, MM-02.H.1–H.3→§20.1–§20.3. **MM-02.H.4 (computable interpreters and agreement) and MM-02.H.5 (instrumented checks) have no counterpart in spec v0**: the interpreter obligations of the brief come from the brief and `formal/DESIGN.md` ("Representation"), not from the spec.

## 0. What P1–P4 are

Not defined in spec v0 (grep: no `P1`…`P4`), nor in `ERN_Jalon3_materiel.md` or `ERN_MM-03.3_v0.4_pour_validation.md`. They are labels of the twelve theorems imposed by the MM-02 v0.2 formalization task, recorded in `formal/reports/MM02_v0.2.md:78-84` (and repeated in `MM02_v0.3.md:121-123`):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract declarations, their docstrings and § citations from Lean files.

Usage: extract.py ROOT FILE... ; writes decls.tsv and cites.tsv next to this script.
"""
import os, re, sys, json

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = sys.argv[1]
FILES = sys.argv[2:]

DECL = re.compile(r'^\s*(?:@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)?(?:(?:private|protected|noncomputable|partial|unsafe|nonrec)\s+)*'
                  r'(def|theorem|lemma|structure|inductive|abbrev|instance|class|opaque|axiom|example)\b\s*([^\s:({\[]*)')
FIELD = re.compile(r'^\s{2,}([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_\'.]*)\s*(?:\{[^}]*\}\s*)?(?:\([^)]*\)\s*)*:')
CTOR = re.compile(r'^\s*\|\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_\'.]*)')
NS = re.compile(r'^\s*namespace\s+(\S+)')
SEC = re.compile(r'^\s*section(?:\s+(\S+))?\s*$')
END = re.compile(r'^\s*end(?:\s+(\S+))?\s*$')

DASH = '[–-]'
def cites(doc):
    """Return set of (sec, item) with item None (whole), int, or '¶p'."""
    out = set()
    # ranges of items §N.k–§M.m or §N.k–m
    for m in re.finditer(r'§(\d+)\.(\d+)[a-z]?\s*' + DASH + r'\s*§?(\d+)(?:\.(\d+))?', doc):
        a, i, b, j = m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3), m.group(4)
        if j is None:  # §N.k–m
            for k in range(int(i), int(b) + 1): out.add((int(a), k))
        elif a == b:
            for k in range(int(i), int(j) + 1): out.add((int(a), k))
        else:
            out.add((int(a), int(i))); out.add((int(b), int(j)))
    # whole-section ranges §N–§M
    for m in re.finditer(r'§(\d+)\s*' + DASH + r'\s*§(\d+)(?![.\d])', doc):
        for k in range(int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)) + 1): out.add((k, None))
    # §N, item(s) k(–m)
    for m in re.finditer(r'§(\d+)(?:\s*,\s*|\s*\(\s*)items?\s+(\d+)(?:\s*' + DASH + r'\s*(\d+))?', doc):
        a, i, j = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), m.group(3)
        for k in range(i, (int(j) if j else i) + 1): out.add((a, k))
    # §N.k
    for m in re.finditer(r'§(\d+)\.(\d+)', doc):
        out.add((int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))))
    # §N ¶p(–¶q)
    for m in re.finditer(r'§(\d+)\s+¶(\d+)(?:\s*' + DASH + r'\s*¶?(\d+))?', doc):
        a, i, j = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), m.group(3)
        for k in range(i, (int(j) if j else i) + 1): out.add((a, '¶%d' % k))
    # bare §N
    for m in re.finditer(r'§(\d+)(?![.\d])', doc):
        out.add((int(m.group(1)), None))
    return out

rows = []
for f in FILES:
    rel = os.path.relpath(f, ROOT)
    lines = open(f, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
    stack = []  # (kind, name)
    doc = None
    in_doc = False
    buf = []
    cur_struct = None  # name of structure/inductive being defined (for fields/ctors)
    i = 0
    for ln, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
        s = line
        if in_doc:
            buf.append(s)
            if '-/' in s:
                in_doc = False
                doc = '\n'.join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        st = s.strip()
        if st.startswith('/--'):
            buf = [s]
            if '-/' in st[3:]:
                doc = s
                buf = []
            else:
                in_doc = True
            # docstring on same line as field: "/-- ... -/ field : T" rare
            continue
        if st.startswith('/-!') or st.startswith('/-'):
            # module doc or comment: skip until closed
            if '-/' not in st[2:]:
                j = ln
                # consume lines
                in_c = True
                # simple: mark to skip lines until -/
                skip_until = True
                # handled by a mini-loop below
                rest = lines[ln:]
                # not needed: comment lines contain no decls typically
            doc = None
            continue
        m = NS.match(s)
        if m:
            stack.append(('ns', m.group(1))); doc = None; cur_struct = None; continue
        m = SEC.match(s)
        if m:
            stack.append(('sec', m.group(1) or '')); doc = None; cur_struct = None; continue
        m = END.match(s)
        if m and st.startswith('end'):
            if stack: stack.pop()
            doc = None; cur_struct = None; continue
        ns = '.'.join(n for k, n in stack if k == 'ns')
        m = DECL.match(s)
        if m and not s.startswith(' ' * 4):
            kind, name = m.group(1), m.group(2)
            if kind == 'instance' and (not name or name.startswith(':')):
                name = '(instance@%d)' % ln
            full = (ns + '.' if ns else '') + name
            rows.append(dict(file=rel, line=ln, kind=kind, name=full, doc=doc or '',
                             cites=sorted(cites(doc or ''), key=str)))
            cur_struct = full if kind in ('structure', 'inductive', 'class') else None
            doc = None
            continue
        if cur_struct and doc is not None:
            m = CTOR.match(s) or FIELD.match(s)
            if m:
                full = cur_struct + '.' + m.group(1)
                rows.append(dict(file=rel, line=ln, kind='field', name=full, doc=doc,
                                 cites=sorted(cites(doc), key=str)))
                doc = None
                continue
        if st and not st.startswith('--') and not st.startswith('@['):
            # any other code line: a pending docstring would be for something unmatched
            if doc is not None and (DECL.match(s) is None):
                pass
        if st == '' and cur_struct is None:
            pass

json.dump(rows, open(os.path.join(HERE, 'decls.json'), 'w'), ensure_ascii=False, indent=0)
print(len(rows), 'declarations')

    lines = open(f, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
    stack = []  # (kind, name)
    doc = None
    in_doc = False
    buf = []
    cur_struct = None  # name of structure/inductive being defined (for fields/ctors)
    i = 0
    for ln, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
        s = line
        if in_doc:
            buf.append(s)
            if '-/' in s:
                in_doc = False
                doc = '\n'.join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        st = s.strip()
        if st.startswith('/--'):
            buf = [s]
            if '-/' in st[3:]:
                doc = s
                buf = []
            else:
                in_doc = True
            # docstring on same line as field: "/-- ... -/ field : T" rare
            continue
        if st.startswith('/-!') or st.startswith('/-'):

            if '-/' not in st[2:]:

                in_c = True

        m = NS.match(s)
        if m:

        m = SEC.match(s)
        if m:
            stack.append(('sec', m.group(1) or '')); doc = None; cur_struct = None; continue
        m = END.match(s)
        if m and st.startswith('end'):
            if stack: stack.pop()
            doc = None; cur_struct = None; continue
        ns = '.'.join(n for k, n in stack if k == 'ns')
        m = DECL.match(s)
        if m and not s.startswith(' ' * 4):
            kind, name = m.group(1), m.group(2)

            full = (ns + '.' if ns else '') + name
            rows.append(dict(file=rel, line=ln, kind=kind, name=full, doc=doc or '',
                             cites=sorted(cites(doc or ''), key=str)))
            cur_struct = full if kind in ('structure', 'inductive', 'class') else None
            doc = None
            continue
        if cur_struct and doc is not None:
            m = CTOR.match(s) or FIELD.match(s)
            if m:
                full = cur_struct + '.' + m.group(1)
                rows.append(dict(file=rel, line=ln, kind='field', name=full, doc=doc,
                                 cites=sorted(cites(doc), key=str)))
                doc = None
                continue
        if st and not st.startswith('--') and not st.startswith('@['):
            # any other code line: a pending docstring would be for something unmatched
            if doc is not None and (DECL.match(s) is None):
                pass
        if st == '' and cur_struct is None:
            pass

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Preserve.Common

/-!
# Arenas: the reference library abstraction (Part XIV)

Arenas of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`, Part XIV (§76–§78), with §36, §46, §55,
§56, §58, §79, §86 and §88. An arena is a library abstraction (Part XIV): its entries live in a
library state separate from the kernel state `S₃` (§38, §46). `newArena` (O17) only registers an
entry; `issue` (O18) and `reset` (O19) are defined twice:

* as their contracts, clause by clause (§77, §78): `IssueC`, `ResetC`;
* as derived operations over the kernel steps (Part XIV): `issue` is its static checks, the
  availability `fail`, then `split` of `internal` on the region and `store` of the block into the
  destination (`IssueD`); `reset` is `derive` of `internal` at `Modify` over the whole storage,
  then `release`, then the explicit check of §78.3 (`ResetD`).

`issue_as_kernel` and `reset_as_kernel` show that both definitions have the same outcomes and the
same arrival states. Library reachability (`LReach`, `LReachNG`) uses the derived operations, so
its kernel states are kernel-reachable (`newArena_as_library`).
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Arena

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! ## Library state (§46) -/

/-- Arena entry (§46): administered storage, `internal` authority, available leaves and issued
regions with their block authorities. The sets of §46 are lists read by membership. -/
structure ArenaEntry where
  storage : Nat
  internal : Nat
  available : List Nat
  issued : List (List Nat × Nat)
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Library state (§46, §38): the kernel state `S₃` and, separately, the arena registry. -/
structure LState where
  kern : S3
  arenas : List ArenaEntry

/-- Initial library state (§47): the initial kernel state and an empty arena registry. -/
def LState.init (statics : Statics) : LState := ⟨S3.init statics, []⟩

/-- Live arena (§46): `internal` is active. -/
def Live (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Prop := s.Active E.internal

/-- Decidability of `Live` (§46). -/
instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Decidable (Live s E) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (s.Active _))

/-- Arena value (§46): the place holding `internal`. -/
def arenaValue (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Option Nat :=
  match s.A[E.internal]? with
  | some y => match y.holder with
    | .place v => some v
    | .frame _ => none
  | none => none

/-- `MetaRight(s, arena)` (§36, §77.1, §78.1): exercisable `Modify` over the arena value; there is
  ancs x`; contained values are covered because their places are usable places (all checked).
- Reset kernel effect: per Part XIV the sequence consumes identity `|A|` and leaves an inactive record
  (`resetKEff`); the contract kernel effect is defined so (§78 states only metadata and "no Init").
- `ResetD` does not check `MetaRight`/liveness itself (they are `derive`'s §60.1, `resetPre_iff`);
  `IssueD` keeps the issue static checks as the task prescribes.
- `LStep.kernel` admits any `KStep` (non-administrative code is unrestricted).

## Not proved / open

- `lInv_kernel` takes `NoDangling` of the post-state (storage usability of a live arena): it is the
  kernel's §57 guarantee, not proved here. With the transfer defect SP-A1 (kernel-defs report), some
  accepted transfers break `NoDangling`, and `lInv_kernel` is then vacuous for them.
- `issue_as_kernel` / `reset_as_kernel` are stated under `KInv` + `ArenaInv` (live entry) hypotheses;
  `lReach_inv` gives `ArenaInv` from the kernel assembly's `WF3 ∧ NoDangling` on reachable states.
- Draft's stronger reuse statement "every past issuance inactive after reset" (incl. empty regions) is
  not proved: it needs a kernel invariant absent from v0 ("an active derived authority held by a place
  p belongs to D p"). The v0 promise (blocks covering recycled leaves) is proved.
- Not rerun on v0 operations: draft witnesses `ce_two_admins`, `ce_two_admins_ok`, `ce_avail_reject`,
  `ce_g2` as a concrete state, H11/H19/H20/H21/W3 and the §79 scenario.
- Cross-registry uniqueness (§56 for HandlePool/DataStack) — registries outside this scope.

## Differences from the draft (Derived/Arena.lean, MM03 arena section)

Registry moved out of `S3` into `LState`; `issue`/`reset` defined twice (contract and derived) instead
of kernel steps; `IssueStaticR` minus "not Init"; O8.5 added to arrival; `ResetPreR` clauses 2/3 per v0
(covering leaf, strict subtree); `MetaRightM` only; `ArenaInv` per §55 (usability added, conjunct 5
split into §55.5 + auxiliary `IssuedShape`); guard over all registries; `issue_v0_as_kernel` /
`reset_v0_as_kernel` scratch proofs ported; `reset_clause3_strict` and
`reset_blocked_by_stored_internal` dropped (false under v0); `arena_reuse_safe` restated.

def descModes (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : List Mode :=
  (List.range s.A.length).filterMap fun j =>
    match s.A[j]? with
    | some y => if y.active = true ∧ p ∈ y.footprint ∧ a ∈ s.ancs j then some y.mode else none
    | none => none

/-- Cases 2–4 of §43 for an active authority of own mode `m` covering the leaf, whose covering
active descendants have modes `ds`. -/
def effOf (m : Mode) (ds : List Mode) : Option Mode :=
  if ds = [] then some m else if Mode.modify ∈ ds then none else some .observe

/-- `effective(s, a, l)` (§43, cases 1–4), computed per leaf. -/
def effective (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : Option Mode :=
  match s.A[a]? with
  | some x => if x.active = true ∧ p ∈ x.footprint then effOf x.mode (descModes s a p) else none
  | none => none

/-- Compatible effective modes for independent ordinary accesses: only `Observe`/`Observe`
(§50). -/
def Compat (m₁ m₂ : Mode) : Prop := m₁ = .observe ∧ m₂ = .observe

/-- Effective mode `e` permits the requested mode `m`: present and not exceeded (§43). -/
def Allows (e : Option Mode) (m : Mode) : Prop := OptP e (fun e => m.le e) False

/-- Decidability of `Allows` (§43). -/
instance (e : Option Mode) (m : Mode) : Decidable (Allows e m) := by
  unfold Allows; infer_instance

/-- Footprint of authority `a` (§42), empty if it does not exist. -/
def S3.afp (s : S3) (a : Nat) : List Nat := match s.A[a]? with
  | some x => x.footprint
  | none => []

/-- Adds an authority with fresh identity `s.A.length` (§42, §60). -/
def S3.addAuth (s : S3) (y : Authority) : S3 := { s with A := s.A ++ [y] }

/-! ## Exercisable authorities (§43) -/

/-- `ExercisableAt(s, a, m)` (§43): `a` is active, its own mode permits `m`, and it is held by
the current frame, or by a place `p` such that an authority itself exercisable at `m` has an
effective mode permitting `m` on every leaf of `p`. Inductive along the holder chain (§43), so no
holder cycle justifies a right. -/
inductive S3.ExercisableAt (s : S3) : Nat → Mode → Prop where
  | base {a : Nat} {m : Mode} {y : Authority} : s.A[a]? = some y → y.active = true → m.le y.mode →
      y.holder = .frame s.top → S3.ExercisableAt s a m
  | held {a p b : Nat} {m : Mode} {y : Authority} : s.A[a]? = some y → y.active = true →
      m.le y.mode → y.holder = .place p → S3.ExercisableAt s b m →
      (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P p, Allows (effective s b l) m) → S3.ExercisableAt s a m

/-- One step of `ExercisableAt · m` read on a Boolean premise (decision procedure for §43). -/
def exR (s : S3) (m : Mode) (E : Nat → Bool) (a : Nat) : Bool :=
  match s.A[a]? with
  | some y => y.active && decide (m.le y.mode) && match y.holder with
    | .frame f => decide (f = s.top)
    | .place p => (List.range s.A.length).any fun b =>
        decide (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P p, Allows (effective s b l) m) && E b
  | none => false

/-- `any` depends only on the values of the predicate on the list (decision procedure for
§43). -/
theorem any_congr' {α : Type} {f g : α → Bool} : ∀ {l : List α}, (∀ b ∈ l, f b = g b) →
    l.any f = l.any g
  | [], _ => rfl
  | a :: l, h => by
    simp only [List.any_cons, h a (List.mem_cons_self ..),
      any_congr' fun b hb => h b (List.mem_cons_of_mem a hb)]

/-- `exR` is a bounded monotone rule (decision procedure for §43). -/
theorem exR_rule (s : S3) (m : Mode) : KRule s.A.length (exR s m) where
  mono p q hpq a h := by
    unfold exR at h ⊢; split at h
    · simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at h ⊢
      refine ⟨h.1, ?_⟩; split at h
      · simpa using h.2
      · simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, List.any_eq_true] at h ⊢
        obtain ⟨b, hb, hc, he⟩ := h.2

/-- `MetaRight(s, arena)` (§36, §77.1, §78.1): exercisable `Modify` over the arena value; there is
no `writeShared` branch. -/
def MetaRight (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Prop :=
  OptP (arenaValue s E) (fun v => HasRight s .modify v) False

/-- Decidability of `MetaRight` (§36). -/
instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Decidable (MetaRight s E) := by
  unfold MetaRight; infer_instance

/-- Available region (§46): each of its leaves belongs to `available`; the empty region is always
available. -/
def Avail (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) : Prop := ∀ l ∈ region, l ∈ E.available

/-- Decidability of `Avail` (§46). -/
instance (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) : Decidable (Avail E region) := by
  unfold Avail; infer_instance

/-! ## `ArenaInv` (§55) -/

/-- `ArenaInv` (§55), required for live arenas. "Still-issued" is read as "with an active block
authority". The clause "anchor and ownership restrictions are respected" has no referent and is
not represented; "complying with exclusivity and validity rules" is left to the kernel
invariants (§57). -/
structure ArenaInv (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Prop where
  /-- §55, item 1: `storage` designates an existing, usable place. -/
  storageUsable : s.Usable E.storage
  /-- §55, item 1: the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`. -/
  fpEq : ∀ l, l ∈ s.afp E.internal ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P E.storage
  /-- §55, item 2: `internal` is active. -/
  active : s.Active E.internal
  /-- §55, item 2: `internal` has own mode `Modify` and is held by a place, the arena value. -/
  shape : OptP (s.A[E.internal]?) (fun y => y.mode = .modify ∧ y.holder.isPlace = true) False
  /-- §55, item 3: available leaves belong to the administered storage. -/
  availableIn : ∀ l ∈ E.available, l ∈ footprint s.P E.storage
  /-- §55, item 3: issued regions belong to the administered storage. -/
  issuedIn : ∀ e ∈ E.issued, ∀ l ∈ e.1, l ∈ footprint s.P E.storage
  /-- §55, item 4: two still-active issuances have disjoint regions. -/
  disjoint : ∀ e ∈ E.issued, ∀ e' ∈ E.issued, e ≠ e' → s.Active e.2 → s.Active e'.2 →
    ∀ l ∈ e.1, l ∉ e'.1
  /-- §55, item 4: no leaf of a still-issued region belongs to `available`. -/
  notAvailable : ∀ e ∈ E.issued, s.Active e.2 → ∀ l ∈ e.1, l ∉ E.available
  /-- §55, item 5: every still-issued block authority is a derivative of `internal`. -/
  derived : ∀ e ∈ E.issued, s.Active e.2 → E.internal ∈ s.ancs e.2

/-- Shape of the issued blocks (support for §55, item 5, from the `ok` effect of §77; not a clause
of `ArenaInv`): every issued block authority exists, has direct origin `internal`, a fresh identity
above it, its region as footprint and mode `Modify`. -/
def IssuedShape (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ E.issued, ∃ y, s.A[e.2]? = some y ∧ y.origin = some E.internal ∧ E.internal < e.2 ∧
    y.footprint = e.1 ∧ y.mode = .modify

/-- The per-entry library invariant (§55): `ArenaInv` and the auxiliary `IssuedShape`. -/
def EntryInv (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Prop := ArenaInv s E ∧ IssuedShape s E

/-- The library invariant (§55, §46): every registered `internal` exists, and every live entry
satisfies `EntryInv`. -/
def LInv (L : LState) : Prop :=
  ∀ E ∈ L.arenas, E.internal < L.kern.A.length ∧ (Live L.kern E → EntryInv L.kern E)

/-! ## O17 `newArena` (§76) and the guard of §56 -/

/-- All leaves of the place holding an authority are `Init` (§76.5); vacuous for a frame. -/
def LeavesInit (s : S3) : Holder → Prop
  | .place v => ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P v, s.I l = .init
  | .frame _ => True

# Report: kernel-main (Access/Main.lean, brief obligation 2)

File: `formal/Ern/MemoryModel/Access/Main.lean` (module `Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main`, 828 lines). It
imports the six Preserve modules and is new and untracked. Nothing was committed, and no other file
was touched.

## Status

- `lake build Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main` succeeds, and so does the full `lake build` (22 jobs,
  including the other agents' current files). `lake env lean` on the file prints nothing, so there
  are no warnings.
- `axcheck.sh Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main` reports 193 constants and 102 theorems. The list outside
  propext and Quot.sound is `#[]`, so there is no Classical.choice.
- The AGENTS.md grep over the whole tree prints nothing. There is no `noncomputable` and no
  `set_option`.
- All 40 declarations have an English docstring that cites a § clause, checked by script. So do the
  constructors of `KernelOp`, `KStar` and `ReachableDU`. There are no draft citations, and no line is
  longer than 100 characters.
- Spec passages read in full before coding: §39, §44, §45, §47, §54, §57, §58, §59, §60–§63, §80.

## Theorems (namespace `Ern.MemoryModel.Access`)

### (e) Operations, steps, reachability, §58, §39

| Name | Statement | Clause |
|---|---|---|
| `KernelOp` (inductive) | the 16 operations O1–O16 with their arguments | §60–§75 |
| `KernelOp.Step k op` (def) | the step relation of the operation, `S3 → Outcome3 S3 → Prop` | §58, §60–§75 |
| `kstep_iff` | `KStep k s s' ↔ ∃ op, op.Step k s (.ok s')` | §57, §58 |
| `KStar k s` (inductive) | reflexive-transitive closure of `KStep` from `s` | §57 |
| `reachable_iff` | `Reachable k statics s ↔ KStar k (S3.init statics) s` | §57 |
| `op_fail_only_alloc` | `op.Step k s .fail → ∃ pr ow ls, op = .alloc pr ow ls` | §58 |
| `kstep_base` | `KStep k s s' → s'.F.getLast? = s.F.getLast?` | §39 |
| `reachable_base` | `Reachable k statics s → s.F.getLast? = some 0`, on every reachable state with no invariant needed | §39, §47 |
| `reachable_base_mem` | `Reachable k statics s → 0 ∈ s.F` | §39 |

### (a) Preservation

| Name | Statement | Clause |
|---|---|---|
| `op_preserves` | `DDSound k → KInv s → KAux s → op.Step k s (.ok s') → (∀ src dst, op ≠ .transfer src dst) → KInv s' ∧ KAux s'` | §57, §58, §60–§75 |
| `kstep_preserves` | over `KStep`: `DDSound k → KInv s → KAux s → KStep k s s' → (KInv s' ∧ KAux s') ∨ ∃ src dst, TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s')` | §57, §58 |
| `op_preserves_heldAnchored` | `WF3 s → HeldAnchored s → op.Step k s (.ok s') → HeldAnchored s'` for **all 16** operations, transfer included | §44, §65, §63, §73 |
| `kstep_preserves_heldAnchored` | the same over `KStep` | §44, §57 |
| `transfer_dst_usable_of_noDangling` | `WF3 s → TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s') → NoDangling s' → s'.Usable dst` | §63.1, §54 |
| `transfer_kinv_iff` | `KInv s → KAux s → HeldAnchored s → TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s') → (KInv s' ∧ KAux s' ↔ s'.Usable dst)` | §57, §63 |
| `op_preserves_of_dst_usable` | `DDSound k → KInv s → KAux s → HeldAnchored s → op.Step k s (.ok s') → (∀ src dst, op = .transfer src dst → s'.Usable dst) → KInv s' ∧ KAux s' ∧ HeldAnchored s'` | §57, §63 |

The strongest true transfer statement is `transfer_kinv_iff`. On states with `KInv ∧ KAux ∧
HeldAnchored`, "destination usable after" is sufficient (the Transfer module's theorem). It is also
**necessary**, because `KInv s'` already gives it through `NoDangling s'`: the §63.1 `Modify`
authority of the current frame over the destination stays active and still covers the destination's
leaves.

### (b) Reachable states

| Name | Statement | Clause |
|---|---|---|
| `reachable_kinv_false` | `¬ ∀ k statics s, DDSound k → StaticsOK statics → Reachable k statics s → KInv s`. Witness: `transfer_breaks_kinv` extended by its transfer step; `StaticsOK cycStatics` is decided. | §57, §63 |
| `KStepDU` (def) | `∃ op, op.Step k s (.ok s') ∧ ∀ src dst, op = .transfer src dst → s'.Usable dst`. The docstring says it is a hypothesis on runs, not a clause of §63 or §57. | §57, §63 |
| `ReachableDU` (inductive) | closure of `KStepDU` from `S3.init statics` | §57 |
| `ReachableDU.reachable` | `ReachableDU ⊆ Reachable` | §57 |
| `kstepDU_iff` | `DDSound k → KInv s → KAux s → HeldAnchored s → (KStepDU k s s' ↔ KStep k s s' ∧ KInv s')` | §57, §63 |
| `reachableDU_kinv` | `DDSound k → StaticsOK statics → ReachableDU k statics s → KInv s ∧ KAux s ∧ HeldAnchored s`, with `KInv = WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan` | §57, §47 |

`kstepDU_iff` shows that the restriction is exactly "the step keeps §57". From a state where the
invariant holds, a kernel step is a `KStepDU` step iff its resulting state satisfies `KInv`. So,
by induction from `init_kinv`, `ReachableDU` is the set of states reached by runs along which §57
holds at every state. This run-level equivalence is not stated as a separate theorem.

### (c) Initial state

| Name | Statement | Clause |
|---|---|---|
| `init_kinv` | `StaticsOK statics → KInv (S3.init statics) ∧ KAux (S3.init statics) ∧ HeldAnchored (S3.init statics)` | §47, §49, §50–§54, §57 |
| `init_statics` | `(S3.init statics).I l = .init ↔ ∃ e, statics[l]? = some e ∧ e.2 = true` | §47, §59 |

### (d) Initialization (§59)

| Name | Statement | Clause |
|---|---|---|
| `KernelOp.Writes s l` (def) | write/writeShared: `l ∈ ls`; store: `l = p`; transfer: `l ∈ footprint s.P dst ∧ ∃ l' ∈ footprint s.P src, corr s.P src dst l' = some l ∧ s.I l' = .init`; every other operation: `False` | §59 |
| `init_only_by_writes` | `op.Step k s (.ok s') → s.I l ≠ .init → s'.I l = .init → op.Writes s l`, keyed on the executed operation | §59 |
| `init_history` | `KStar k (S3.init statics) s → s.I l = .init → (∃ e, statics[l]? = some e ∧ e.2 = true) ∨ ∃ t t' op, KStar k (S3.init statics) t ∧ op.Step k t (.ok t') ∧ t.I l ≠ .init ∧ t'.I l = .init ∧ op.Writes t l ∧ KStar k t' s` (an explicit run init →* t → t' →* s) | §47, §59 |

Private helpers: `heldAnchored_of_step` (the shared argument: §49.8 gives a usable holder before
the step), `getElem?_append_cases`, `initP_len`, `initP_get`, `initP_get'`, `initA_get`,
`rootIdx_get`, `statics_parent`, `statics_owner`, `init_usable`, `init_lt_of_mem_footprint`,
`init_rootPlace`, `init_root_inj`. Reused from other modules: `Frames.getElem?_inj_of_lt`,
`Frames.range_pairwise_lt`, `Frames.exists_getElem?_of_mem`, `EndFree.endUse_active`,
`EndFree.free_active`, and `Alloc.guarded_ne_fail`. No forbidden list lemma is used.

## HeldAnchored: the conjecture holds

`HeldAnchored` holds at `S3.init`, since there is no derived authority. It is preserved by every
kernel step from a `WF3` state (`op_preserves_heldAnchored`). No counterexample exists for any
operation:

- **derive, split, enterFrame, alloc:** new authorities are frame-held or have no origin.
  `enterFrame` parameters become frame-held.
- **release:** filters only the released anchor.
- **depend:** only adds anchors.
- **store:** anchors the stored authority (§65 effect).
- **transfer:** the Transfer module's theorem.
- **exitFrame:** a surviving anchor maps to itself (`firstSurv (x :: ancs x) = x`).
- **endUse:** an authority that stays active is not held within `p`, so its holder's `D` is kept.
- **free:** keeps `D`.
- **read, write, writeShared, pin, unpin:** keep `A` and `D`.

So P-T2 (Transfer report) cannot occur on `ReachableDU` states. Its counterexample `ahx` is not
reachable by such runs.

## Obligations not proved

None. One point is open, and nothing needs it: whether `HeldAnchored` holds on **every**
`Reachable` state. The preservation proof uses `WF3` before the step, and `WF3` fails after the
ownership-cycle transfer.

## Readings (representation only)

1. **"Every step except transfer" over unlabelled `KStep`** is stated as a disjunction
   (`kstep_preserves`: preserved, or the step is an accepted transfer). Over the labelled
   operations it is `op ≠ .transfer` (`op_preserves`). A hypothesis such as "not a transfer step"
   on `KStep` would exclude pairs `(s, s')` that both a transfer and another operation produce.
   The disjunction avoids that.
2. **§59 "permitted write"** is keyed on the executed operation, not existentially over the
   operations relating `s` and `s'`. "Including during a derived `issue`" is covered by `store`,
   because `issue` is a library operation. The transfer disjunct is read as the draft reads it: a
   destination leaf with a corresponding source leaf `Init` before the step.
3. **§59 global form (`init_history`).** It is stated over an explicit run (`KStar`) through a
   witness step `t → t'`. It does not assert that the leaf stays `Init` after `t'`, or throughout
   in the declared case. That stronger history form was not requested.
4. **§39 "the base frame, whose identity is 0 in states reachable from the initial state, never
   exits"** is read as: the bottom of the stack is 0 on every reachable state
   (`reachable_base`). It needs no invariant, because only `exitFrame` pops a frame and §73.1
   requires a caller.
5. **§58 "only `alloc` may produce `fail`"** is stated over `KernelOp.Step`. "Leaving the state
   unchanged" holds by representation: `Outcome3.fail` carries no state. This is kernel-defs
   reading 47.
6. **`KAux` and `HeldAnchored`** are auxiliary invariants carried through the induction. Neither
   is a clause of §57. Both are discharged on the reachable states of `reachableDU_kinv`, whose
   conclusion contains `KInv` exactly.

## Problems found / for arbitration

- **P-M1 (= SP-A1 / P-T1, now at the level of §57).** §57 is false as stated
  (`reachable_kinv_false`). The witness satisfies both of §57's hypotheses, `DDSound` and
  well-formed statics. The exact repair, on states where the auxiliary invariants hold, is "the
  transfer destination is usable in the resulting state" (`transfer_kinv_iff`). This is the
  draft's dropped clause. Adding it to §63 as a precondition would make `reachableDU_kinv` the
  unconditional §57.
- **P-M2 (P-T2 resolved for these runs).** The §63.7 gap only matters on states without
  `HeldAnchored`. `HeldAnchored` is an invariant along every `KStepDU` run, so with the P-M1 repair
  §63.7 as written suffices.
- **§47 statics (P2, recorded).** `init_kinv` and `reachableDU_kinv` take `StaticsOK` as a
  hypothesis that §47 does not state. Review finding F2 notes that `StaticsOK` (`ShapeOK 0`) also
  requires owners to precede the statics they own. That is stronger than acyclicity, so it narrows
  the domain of the init theorems to declarations listed owner-first.

§63.1–§63.8 hold: both usable, exercisable `Modify` on 0 (root 0) and on 3 (root 3 via root 2 via root 0); same shape (single leaves); `src` Init, 3 Uninit, disjoint; no pins, no anchors; authority 2 (held by part `src`) moves to `corr(src) = 3` and its footprint `[2]` contains no leaf of 3 (§63.8); in the result place 3 is not usable, so `AnchorOrderHeld` is vacuous for it. Lean confirms every draft `TransferPre` clause except the draft-only `(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst` (MM03:1247).
Result: place 2 is owned by 3 and 3 by 2; authority 2 is active, held by the unusable place 3 (§49.8 false) and covers leaf 2 of the unusable place 2 (`NoDangling` false); under the global reading of §49.3 (P3) the cycle also violates WF3.3. The draft rejects the step only through its own clause, which has no spec text. Not a charter §4.1 violation (authorities 2 and 3 are no longer exercisable: `ExercisableAt` is inductive and the holder chain is cyclic; the storage leaks, which charter §4.1 permits), but the §57 guarantee is false for the spec as written. Needed decision: e.g. require the destination usable in the resulting state, or read §63.7 as requiring every moved authority's new holder to have a frame.

**P2: well-formedness of the declared statics is not stated (§47, §57).**
§47: "a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter." Nothing excludes cycles or a part owned differently from its parent. Example (`check/Stat.lean`): statics 0 owned by 1 and 1 owned by 0: in `S3.init`, authority 0 is active and held by place 1, and places 0 and 1 are unusable, so §49.8 fails in the initial state and "reachable ⇒ WF3" (§57) is false. The draft adds `ShapeOK` (owners and parents are earlier statics, a part has its parent's owner) as a premise of `Reachable.init`; it is a representation of "well-formed declaration" only if the spec says statics are well-formed.

**P3: scope of "well-founded" in §49.3.**
"valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place" reads either (A) all ownership chains are well-founded, and those of usable places reach a live frame, or (B) for every usable place, its chain is well-founded and reaches a live frame. Under (B) the clause is implied by the inductive `Usable` and adds nothing; under (A) the state `DraftGaps.wf_cyc` (MM23.lean:3899, two places owning each other, no authority) violates WF3. v0.4 FR "des chaînes de possession bien fondées, qui atteignent un cadre vivant pour chaque emplacement utilisable" leans to (A); MM23_v0.1.md (f) 6 used (A). The planned "WF3 gains well-founded ownership" presupposes (A). Under (A), P1 also breaks WF3.3.

**P4: §59.b anchor list vs §69 effect.**
§59: "Access operations do not change an anchor without an explicitly authorized effect of transfer, `depend`, `store`, release, or reanchoring." §69 effect: "dependencies of the ended value are removed" while "`place` **remains usable as a place**". Example: `store a p` gives `D(p) = [a]`; `endUse p` makes `D(p) = []` with `p` usable (draft `endUseS` MM03:3937 does this). If "access operations" means all kernel operations, §59 forbids what §69 prescribes (endUse is not in the list; nor is the clearing of `D` by `free`, draft `freeS` MM03:4101, which §70 does not state). If it means O9–O11 only, there is no conflict. The statement of a §59 anchor theorem depends on the reading.

**P5: "valid origin" in §51 is undefined, and decides whether `endUse` preserves I2.**
§51: "Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules." §44 defines validity for anchors only ("valid as long as the authority it names is active"). Example (`check/EU.lean`, reached): frame 1 locals X (0, Init) and p (1); derive 2 from root 0 on X (`Modify`); `store 2 p`; derive 3 from 2 on X (held by frame 1). `endUse p`: §69.2 concerns descendants "over the leaves of `place` or storage that dies with it" (3 covers X, which does not die), §69.3 holds once `p`'s dependencies are removed, §69.4 no pins; so the spec accepts it, and the effect releases 2 (held by `p`) while 3 stays active with origin 2 inactive. If "valid origin" means active, I2 fails after an accepted step; if it means existing, I2 holds, and the draft's extra `EndUseAccessOK` disjunct "`∃ a ∈ s.ancs j, EndUseReleased s p a`" (MM03:3979), which rejects this step (Lean 

**P6 (silence): the footprint of a root authority is never stated.**
§40 "Every root place has a root authority of own mode `Modify`, with no origin, held exactly by that place's owner"; §47, §49.6–7, §71, §72 never say it covers `footprint(r)`. The draft fixes `footprint (P) r` (`S3.init`, `enterEff`, `allocEff`, `RootLive`, `RootChain`). A smaller footprint would change accepted programs (`HasRight` on fresh storage fails) and makes `NoOrphan` underivable from `WF3` (`chain_to_frame` uses `z.footprint = footprint r`). The natural reading is `footprint(r)`; it needs confirmation, not a choice.

No contradiction with the charter found in this scope (P1 produces a leak and broken invariants, not an exercisable access).

---

## 5. Representation choices (no accepted program changes)

1. `Reachable` as the closure of one `Step` relation (`init` + `step`), `Step` = the ok-outcomes of O1–O16; `read` keeps the state. Makes (i) definitional.
2. Labelled steps: `inductive Op` (as HandlePool.lean:1535) and `OpStep k : Op → S3 → Outcome → Prop`, `Step k s s' := ∃ o, OpStep k o s (.ok s')`; `WrittenBy` keyed on the executed `o`; executions as lists of `(Op, S3)` for (h).

# Report — key `refinement`

File: `formal/Ern/MemoryModel/Refinement.lean` (module `Ern.MemoryModel.Refinement`, namespace
`Ern.MemoryModel.Refinement`, imports `Ern.MemoryModel.Machine` and
`Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Preserve.Common`). New, untracked, nothing committed. No other file touched.

## Status

- `lake build Ern.MemoryModel.Refinement`: success. `lake env lean` on the file: no warning.
- `axcheck.sh Ern.MemoryModel.Refinement`: 750 constants, 357 theorems, list outside
  propext/Quot.sound `#[]` (no `Classical.choice`).
- No `sorry`/`admit`/`native_decide`/`axiom`/`noncomputable`/`set_option`. Every declaration has
  an English docstring citing a § (checked by script); no draft citation (no MM-0x, K1–K5, L1–L8,
  pass names, SP labels); no line over 100 characters.
- Concrete runs are checked by `decide` (kernel-checked, a few seconds in all).

## Theorems proved (clause)

Representation (§82.1, §82.3–§82.5, §9, §23):
- `LayoutWF` (fields `parts`, `disjoint`, `within`), `Repr` (fields `adm : Machine.Admissible`,
  `layout`, `inj`, `tokens`, `live`, `init`). `Repr.adm` is the reference Machine's §9
  admissibility (freshness, live disjointness, alignment), not freshness alone.
- `Repr.transport`, `Repr.same_places`, `Repr.of_eqs`, `repr_extend` (new places), `repr_base`.

R1, R2 (§82.2, §66–§68, §15, §16):
- `r1_read`: under `Repr`, `WF3`, `Read3Pre`, each leaf read has a live allocation with initialized
  range and `ReadStep … (.ok bytes)` given its parametric obligations. No `NoDangling`/`FpLeaves`
  hypothesis (usability comes from §66.1).
- `r6_read`, `r2_write`, `r2_writeShared`, `writes_ok`, `writes_repr`: raw reads/writes are an
  `Exec` of `ok` steps and `Repr` holds after (any written representation `w`).

R6 for every kernel operation O1–O16 (§82 preamble, §82.4, §82.5): `r6_derive`, `r6_split`,
`r6_release`, `r6_depend`, `r6_pin`, `r6_unpin`, `r6_endUse` (no raw op), `r6_read`, `r2_write`,
`r2_writeShared`, `r6_transfer` (copies: read source leaf, write its bytes into `corr` leaf),
`r6_store`, `r6_enter` (one `AllocStep` per root local), `r6_exit` (one `DeallocStep` per root
directly owned by the exiting frame; those allocations dead afterwards), `r6_free` (one
`DeallocStep`; dead afterwards), `r6_alloc` (exactly one `AllocStep`, by `oneRoot`),
`r6_alloc_fail` (no op, §58). Uniform form: `r6` (any `OpStep` from a state with `WF3 ∧
NoDangling`, under `ParamsOK` and `StepObl`).

R4 (§82.5, §54, §52): `r4_no_dead_cover` (an active authority covers only leaves with live
allocations containing their range), `r4_anchors` (anchors of usable places active, their leaves'
storage live).

Allocation/deallocation contracts (§82.4, §17, §80): `freeSound_derived` (under `Repr`, `WF3`,
`NoDangling`, `FreePre`, and `K.FreeCompat → FreeCompatInst`, the raw deallocation has
`CanDealloc`), `deallocable_sound`, `placement_exists`, `topPlacement_ok`, zero size `runZ_sim`.

Pointers (§82.2, §82.3; address rules of the brief): `ptrAddr`, `anchorAlloc`, `storeOps`,
`pointer_sound_store` (range of the target decodes to the address, every byte carries the
provenance of the effective anchor's allocation; every region leaf is in that live allocation;
empty region → base of that allocation; otherwise the lowest address among leaves of nonzero
size), `anchorAlloc_eq`, `effAnchor_footprint`, `chainF_last`.

Disjointness (§23, §82.1, §82.8): `byteDisjoint_of_leaves` (decision 1 direction: leaf disjointness
⇒ byte disjointness under `LayoutWF`), `declaredDisjoint_bytes` (under `DDSound`),
`exclusive_bytes`. No instantiation of `DeclaredDisjoint` by bytes.

Pinning (§82.6): `pinned_address_stable` (for every realized step, a pinned leaf whose allocation
is live before keeps a live allocation and the same address; free/exit cases use §70.4/§73.3).

Simulation (§82 preamble): `SimRun` (init with `StaticsOK`, statics layout, init write
obligations; each step: `WF3 s ∧ NoDangling s` on the pre-state, `OpStep`, `StepObl`), with
`k`, `C`, `ObR`, `ObW`, `statics`, `π : Params` fixed once. `simulation`: `Exec` from
`State.empty`, `Repr`, `Access.Reachable`. `repr_init` for the statics.

Non-vacuity / concrete runs (decide): `runD_sim` (16 steps: enter, write, pin, unpin, alloc,
transfer, endUse, writeShared, depend, derive, write, read, store, release, free, exit; `Repr`,
`LayoutWF` of a concrete layout, `ParamsOK`, freed and local allocations dead, static live),
`runZ_sim` (zero-size allocation), `H15`, `H16`, `pinned_not_usable_after_transfer`.
Supporting: `WF3Check`/`wf3_of_check`, `NoDanglingCheck`/`noDangling_of_check`,
`kInv_kAux_of_check`, runner `srun`/`srun_sound`, `sim_of`.

## Corpus H15/H16

Both pass, encoded at kernel level (`issue` = `split` then `store`, Part XIV preamble), with
`Repr` on the final state:
- `H15`: leaf 2 (empty block split from root 5) decodes to 88 = base of allocation of place 5,
  provenance `some 5` on all 8 bytes; leaf 4 (empty region split from root of local 3) decodes to
  56 = base of allocation of 3, provenance `some 3`; bases nonzero.
- `H16`: region `[5, 4]` (offsets 8, 0) decodes to 56 = base of allocation of 3 (leaf 4), not
  base + 8.
Next wave (corpus/arena): re-encode both through the library `issue` of `Ern.MemoryModel.Arena`;
since `issue` is `split` then `store`, the bytes must be identical (expansion of library steps
into `opsOf` of their kernel steps).

## Not proved / open

1. Derived arena operations (§82.7, §76–§78): not covered (Arena module not available at start).
   Needed next wave: a library-step relation expanded into `KOp` lists; realization = concatenated
   `opsOf`; R6 from `r6` per kernel step; `issue fail` → no op; `newArena` → no op; §82.7d (no
   access after reset) as a theorem over `r4_no_dead_cover` + reset precondition.
2. `store` of a nonempty region whose leaves all have size zero (§82.3): no address rule recorded
   (map problem P5). `ptrAddr = none`; `r6_store` and `StepObl` require `PtrDecided` (documented
   as not a spec clause). Arbitration needed.
3. §82.3 `Init` ↔ valid representation of the type (map change 7): not represented; `Repr.init`
   is initialization only; type validity stays in the parametric `dec`/`stat` obligations.
4. §82.6 physical obligations of statics and external use: no dedicated theorem (statics are
   frame-0 roots with a recorded token; never deallocated unless frame 0 exits).
5. Value content of `transfer` (destination bytes = source bytes): not stated (only `ok` + `Repr`).
6. Leaf/type alignment is not in the layout interface (left to §15.6/§16.5 obligations).

## Readings and representation choices

- Layout over every place index (`Layout := Nat → Machine.Place`); non-leaf places only use
  `alloc`; `parts` clause (a part is in its parent's allocation).
- One allocation per root place, distinct (`inj`): excludes realizations where several roots share
  one allocation (e.g. a data stack, §9 ¶5); existence of one realization suffices for §82.
- Tokens indexed by root place (`rtok r`), statics included. `FreeCompatInst C rtok p auth :=
  C auth (rtok p)`; `ParamsOK` requires `C (rtok r) (rtok r)` (automatic deallocation at exit
  presents the recorded token). Consequence: every root is deallocatable (`deallocable_sound`);
  `K.Deallocable` is not otherwise used.
- `exitFrame` deallocates the allocations of root places directly owned by the exiting frame and
  not marked dead (`exitRoots`); storage they own leaks (§73 "does not entail automatic physical
  deallocation of all dead places"). Whether automatic storage must be deallocated is not fixed by
  the spec (problem 3 below).
- `free` deallocates the allocation of the place only; owned storage leaks (§70 effect).
- `endUse`: no raw operation (§69).
- `transfer`: per corresponding leaf pair, a read then a write of the bytes read, provenance
  included (realization chosen for §10 ¶6, not a propagation rule).
- Reference encoding: `PtrEnc` with `size`, `enc`, `decode` and field `reads` (decode reads only
  `size` bytes); `PtrEncAt` is a per-pointer obligation (finite width, Spec 11); target of pointer
  size is a stated hypothesis of `pointer_sound_store`. Provenance of every reference = allocation
  of the effective anchor (for nonempty regions this equals the leaves' allocation,
  `anchorAlloc_eq`).
- Obligations `dec ∧ stat` along each sequence (`OblAlong`), not a global `stat`.
- Run invariant hypotheses: `WF3 ∧ NoDangling` (the parts of `KInv` used); stronger than taking
  `KInv`; `KAux` is not needed by any realization.
- `NewLayout.leaves` states that each new leaf is in a new root's allocation (derivable from the
  other clauses; kept as a decidable obligation).

## Problems found

1. §82.3: address of a reference to a nonempty region of zero-size leaves (above, item 2).
2. §74 / §63.5 with the transfer cycle (§63 vs §49.8): a pinned usable leaf becomes unusable after
   an `ok` `transfer`, from a reachable state with `KInv ∧ KAux` (`pinned_not_usable_after_transfer`,
   decided: statics 0, 1; `alloc 1 0`, `alloc 1 2`, `pin 2`, then `transfer 0 3`). "Pinned leaves
   stay usable" is therefore not an invariant of the reference kernel; `pinned_address_stable` is
   stated on allocation liveness and does not depend on it.
3. §73: the spec does not say whether the automatic storage of exiting locals is deallocated
   (only that not all dead places are); the chosen realization deallocates direct frame roots.
4. §23 `LayoutWF` has no clauses in the spec; defined here by §82.1/§23 needs (map P1).

   `SimRun` policy (invariant as hypothesis, transfer can break it). The intermediate kernel states
   inside `issue`/`reset` get them by the committed preservation lemmas: no extra hypothesis.

/-- §82.7 for translated library runs: the derived operations and their metadata, outside `S₃`,
are realized by O1–O16 without reintroducing access after invalidation. The run is a labelled
library run from the initial library state; its memory state is reached from the initial memory
state by the raw operations of its kernel steps (the machine trace of the run is the trace of its
kernel steps); and after every legal `reset` in the run, no kernel step of the continuation uses
an authority derived from `internal` that covered a leaf of the administered storage, so no raw
operation of the continuation is an access through it. -/
theorem arena_realized {Ty : Type} {k : K} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {statics : Statics} {π : Params Ty} {L : LState}
    {s2 : Machine.State} (h : LSimRun k C ObR ObW statics π L s2) :
    ∃ t, LPath k (LState.init statics) t L ∧
      s2 = run (minit π statics) (ktrace π (ltrace t) (minit π statics)) ∧
      ∀ t₁ t₂ L₀ i E, t = t₁ ++ (.reset i, L₀) :: t₂ → L₀.arenas[i]? = some E →

**How to apply:** start a new pass from the latest branch tip; run an adversarial review workflow over module and report before delivering; `lake` is not on PATH, call `~/.elan/bin/lake`; keep the Lake library name `Ern`. `formal/Ern/.gitkeep` keeps showing as deleted: restore it with `git checkout`, never commit the deletion. A post-commit hook can make `git commit` exceed 2 minutes: give it a long timeout. The axiom rule ({propext, Quot.sound} only) forbids core lemmas that pull `Classical.choice` (`List.getElem?_mapIdx`, `List.eq_nil_iff_forall_not_mem`, `List.nodup_range`, `List.pairwise_lt_range`): sweep `#print axioms` over every theorem and replace them with local lemmas. Mathlib tactics (`set`, `tauto`) are unavailable. Reviews keep catching report errors: quote old forms from the old commit, count declarations with a command, and base an evidence claim only on a check that would fail on the defect. After fixing review findings, run a second targeted review of the fixes: in MM-03 pass 2 a fix over-rejected legitimate programs. Before calling a clause "missing" from an arbitrage, re-read every earlier arbitrage still in force: in pass 3 the clause needed for exitFrame_no_dangling was A4's root-holder rule, which A1 puts in WF3 and pass 2 had left out. `timeout` does not exist on this Mac: run `lake build` directly (about 2.5 min). When an arbitrage enlarges a definition used in hypotheses (pass 4: `Inv3` gained `NoDangling`), theorems whose text is unchanged silently narrow: give them only the conjunct they use. Before retiring a counterexample whose witness breaks a new invariant clause, look for another witness: pass-4 review found one and flagged the weakening as major. Check obligations against the initial state: the base frame of `S3.init` owns no place, so an obligation about it can be vacuous on reached states. A review fix can itself pick a semantic reading (pass 5: the kind conjunct of `IsInternalFor` rejected a `newArena` that D3 leaves undecided): check every fix for verdicts it changes on cases the text is silent on. Module docstrings must cite the report's own numbering, not the review's decision numbers. Arbiter-supplied theorems can be false: check them on small reached states (owned storage, a parameter that is the ancestor of another) before trying a proof. Every factual claim in the report needs a module witness, or reviewers flag it; never say "blocked until X" without checking escape sequences such as ending the owner value. When a precondition gains clauses, lemmas taking it as a hypothesis narrow silently: name the old precondition (pass 7: `EnterPreBase`) and give the lemmas only what they use. A guard on one operation (G2 on `store`) is usually bypassable through another (a helper authority then `release`/`endUse`/`free`/exit): look for such bypasses before claiming a configuration is excluded. A new check on an operation with a defined failure (`issue` → `fail`) must not turn that failure into `reject`. Use one adversarial reviewer per arbitrage lens; each found distinct real issues in pass 7. When a restriction rejects an old counterexample, try to rebuild a witness that satisfies the new clause before restating it as a rejection (pass 8: a same-shape destination restored `transfer_not_inv3_preserving`). Drop hypotheses a proof does not use. When cases disappear because their state is no longer reached, replay their verdicts on a new reachable state and list the drops. Machine-check every changed verdict the report lists, including the old witnesses' rejected steps. Never state "only clause X fails" as `X → Pre` next to `¬ X`: that is vacuous; name the other clauses (pass 8: `TransferPreBase` with an iff) and state them. Run a second targeted check after fixing verification findings: in pass 8 it caught that vacuous form. `omega` proving a conjunction goal pulls `Classical.choice`: split the goal first. `meta` is a keyword in this Lean: never name a hypothesis `meta`. `set` (Mathlib) is unavailable: use `obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ : ∃ x, x = e := ⟨_, rfl⟩`. `if_pos`/`if_neg`/`ite_cond_eq_true` are deprecated: use `simp only [h, ↓reduceIte]`. When `S3.Usable.mono` is applied with `rfl` for `hP`, give `(s := …) (s' := …)` explicitly or it unifies the wrong way. Simulation theorems: never quantify obligations over all translations (vacuous); put them as per-step premises of the run with parameters fixed once, and give a concrete multi-step run as witness. A universal encoding obligation (`∀ addr, decode (enc addr) = addr`) is unsatisfiable by a finite computable decode: state it per value. `lake env lean` uses the last built olean: rebuild the module before a scratch file uses new declarations. Never use an unquoted heredoc for Lean or docstrings: backticks run as shell commands; use `<<'EOF'` and pass paths by environment variable. `example`s escape a `collectAxioms` sweep: rename them to theorems in a scratch copy to check their axioms. `awk length` counts bytes, not characters: count line length in Python. Each check round finds errors in the previous round's wording: when a sentence is fixed in a docstring, grep the report for the same claim; quote arbitrages exactly (L2 said "hypothèse des énoncés", not "hors langage"); classify every item a deliverable asks to classify instead of moving it aside; a summary must not present a hypothesis restated in a conclusion as a result. Count theorem constants with internal ones (`isInternal`) and say which count you give. A callee cannot move a value out of a parameter's footprint (`ActiveDerivedOutside` counts the parameter itself): build values to transfer as callee locals. Authority ids shift with every alloc/issue/split: check them with `#eval` of `prun` prefixes before writing a case. A literal invariant from the material can fail under the full kernel extension: keep the literal statement with counterexamples and prove the parts that hold, under their own names. A runner's fallback state must be unreachable (e.g. no frame) or a statement "the run's state is reached" is vacuous when the run fails; give a lemma deriving success from reachability. Projecting `.2` out of an existential passes the elaborator but fails in the kernel: use `obtain`. When `step_ok_of`-style lemmas time out at `whnf`, pass the contract `k` and statics explicitly. Jalon 3 took four check rounds (11/9/9/4 confirmed): each round's fixes need their own narrow check. The list `Sublist` notation `<+` is scoped: write `List.Sublist`; `List.take_add` pulls `Classical.choice`. `omit … in` goes before the docstring. A `def` in a `variable (k : K)` section takes `k` only if it uses it: check call sites. In a multi-line `{ st with … }`, put each field on its own line at one column. Theorems stated for registered arenas (`ar ∈ s.arenas`) do not carry over to library instances: never cite them for one. Before writing "the only effect of X is Y", look for a witness in the other direction (derivability: the missing guard also turned a `fail` into an `ok`).

/-- Releases every authority whose holder is no longer live (§69, §70 `ok` effects). -/
def cleanup (s : S3) : S3 :=
  { s with A := s.A.map fun y => if HolderLive s y.holder then y else { y with active := false } }

/-! ## O12 `endUse` (§69) -/

/-- `endUse p` before releasing authorities whose holder died (§69, `ok` effect): the leaves of
`p` become `Uninit`; authorities held within `p` are released; anchors of `p` and its parts are
removed; storage owned by `p`, transitively, is marked dead. -/
def endUseS (s : S3) (p : Nat) : S3 :=
  { s with
    I := fun l => if l ∈ footprint s.P p then .uninit else s.I l
    D := fun q => if partOf s.P q p then [] else s.D q
    dead := fun q => s.dead q || decide (OwnedIn s.P p q)
    A := s.A.map fun y => if heldIn s.P p y.holder then { y with active := false } else y }

/-- Effect of `endUse p` (§69, `ok` effect): `endUseS`, then the authorities whose holder died
are released. -/
def endUseEff (s : S3) (p : Nat) : S3 := cleanup (endUseS s p)

/-- Leaf whose use ends with the value at `p` (§69.2, §69.4): a leaf of `p` or of storage that
